title: EMR and Glue processing choices
scenario: Brackenridge Fisheries Co-op processes boat and cannery data on three fronts. Every night a 14 TB Spark job written in Scala runs for about 10 hours; it needs a vendor's native compression library installed on every worker and memory-heavy instance types that its engineers pick themselves. Two bookkeepers, who do not write code, must fix blank values, odd date formats and outliers in about 30 supplier spreadsheets a week before the data is loaded. Eight analysts run SQL over the cleaned files in Amazon S3 a few times a week and expect results in minutes.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
Only the nightly job may justify capacity that runs for hours; nothing else may need a cluster that staff size, start or patch
The bookkeepers will not learn a scripting language
Finance pays for analyst queries only when they run
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions

rubric.label: Why live lab was unsuitable documented
Each of the three workloads is given a compute option whose management burden matches its stated need, with the custom library and instance-type control provided only where the scenario asks for them
The bookkeepers' cleaning and the analysts' SQL both run with no code from the bookkeepers and no cluster to manage, and the cleaned output is queryable without anyone hand-writing table definitions

constraint_reason: Service unavailable or not disposable in a personal same-day lab
